body_long:
Accor is buying out its partners in Ennismore. On Tuesday 17 November 2026, the French group announced an agreement to acquire 44.3% of the fully diluted share capital of its lifestyle platform for about €1.6 billion, from founder Sharan Pasricha and Q Lifestyle Company Ltd, the Qatari investor.

## The deal

The shares will change hands in three tranches: 25.4% by the end of January 2027, 6.3% by July 2027 and 12.6% by January 2028. The price values Ennismore's equity at about €3.7 billion, around 18 times its expected 2027 EBITDA. According to Skift, that is more than double the company's value four years ago, when Accor sold a 10.8% stake to a Qatari consortium.

Accor will fund the purchase with at least €500 million from speeding up the sale of non-strategic assets, an additional credit line and an option to pay part of the price in Accor shares. The group says its €500 million share buyback, linked to the sale of its Essendi stake, stays on track, and so does its investment-grade rating.

Sharan Pasricha, who founded Ennismore and ran it for fifteen years, stays on its board. Sébastien Bazin, Chairman and CEO of Accor, calls Ennismore "a strategic pillar of the Group".

## The platform

Accor and Ennismore combined their lifestyle brands in 2021. The company now gathers Mama Shelter, The Hoxton, SLS, Mondrian, Rixos, Faena and Paris Society: nearly 200 hotels and more than 800 restaurants and bars in 40 countries, with a further 150 hotels in the pipeline.

Gaurav Bhushan has led it alone since January 2026, when Ennismore ended its co-CEO model.

The weight of the platform explains the price. Ennismore holds about 5% of Accor's rooms, but about 20% of its recurring EBITDA and some 40% of its EBITDA growth over the last three years.

## What comes next

There is no stock market listing for now. Accor says it keeps exploring ways to speed up Ennismore's growth, including new strategic partners or a public listing.

## The signal

Per room, lifestyle earns about four times the group average at Accor. Restaurants, bars and strong brands now carry the value, and Accor is paying to keep all of it in-house before deciding whether to share it again.
summary: Accor will buy 44.3% of Ennismore from Sharan Pasricha and Q Lifestyle Company for about €1.6bn, in three tranches to January 2028. Equity value: about €3.7bn.
title: Accor buys out its partners in Ennismore for €1.6bn
